transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you to the clinic?

My thoughts feel all jumbled and I can’t keep my words or plans straight anymore, even for simple tasks I’ve done for years. Between working full-time and caring for my sick husband, I got so overwhelmed recently that I left several cleaning jobs half-finished and even got lost driving a route I know by heart. My employer and my pastor were so worried about me that they urged me to come get some help.
Did these problems start after a specific stressful event or life change, or have they been gradually getting worse over time?

It all really started about a year and a half ago when my husband developed severe complications from his diabetes and I had to become his main caregiver. Since then, with all the added stress, these problems have been gradually building and getting much worse over the last year.
Have you had any memory or thinking problems before your husband became ill, or did these difficulties start only after the stress of caring for him began?

No, I never had any problems like this before; I used to have a very ordered life with meticulous checklists and reliable judgment. These jumbled thoughts and planning difficulties only started building up about a year after his health got really bad and the caregiving stress piled up.
Have these thinking and memory problems improved at all when your stress is lighter, or do they stay about the same no matter what is happening around you?

To be honest, because my husband has been so sick and I'm caregiving constantly, I haven't really had a time when the stress was any lighter. It's hard to tell if it would improve, because these jumbled thoughts and confusion just feel like they are pretty much always there now.
When you get a break from caregiving or the stress is lower, do your thinking and memory problems noticeably improve, or do they stay the same?

I don't really get much of a break from the caregiving or the stress to know for sure. Even on the rare days when things quiet down briefly, my mind still feels just as jumbled, so I'm not sure if it actually improves at all.
Have you had any head injury, stroke, seizure, new medical illness, or started any new medications around the time these thinking problems began?
No, nothing like that has happened to me. I haven't had any head injuries, strokes, or seizures, and I haven't started any new medications or been diagnosed with any new illnesses of my own.
Have these problems with memory, attention, or planning been present continuously for at least 6 months, or do they mainly come and go with periods of stress?

Yes, they have been present continuously for a bit over a year now, rather than just coming and going. While the caregiving stress definitely started it, this confusion and trouble keeping my thoughts straight has become a constant, daily battle for over twelve months.
Do your thinking and memory problems clearly get better when the stress is reduced, or do they stay about the same even when you have a break from caregiving?

I haven't really had a true break from caregiving because my husband's health is a constant worry. Even during the brief, quieter weeks when I'm not as revved up or rushing around, my thoughts still feel quite jumbled and I don't feel like my old steady self.
Do your thinking and memory problems clearly get better when the caregiving stress is reduced, or do they stay about the same even when you have a break?

Like I mentioned, I haven't really had a proper break from caregiving since my husband's health got bad, so I'm not sure if it would get better. Right now, the jumbled thoughts and confusion just feel constant no matter what.

Have these thinking and memory problems caused you to make mistakes at work or in daily life that are clearly worse than before, such as getting lost, missing bills, or needing help with tasks you used to do independently?

Yes, it's caused terrible mistakes, like leaving several client homes half-cleaned and getting completely lost driving a route I've known for years. I've also become so scattered that I skip meals and even forget basic things like showering or taking my own medicine. It's just so overwhelming because I can't keep up with anything anymore.

Did these thinking and memory problems start only after the caregiving stress began, or did you have any similar difficulties before that? Also, have they been steadily present even when the stress briefly eases?

Yes, they only started after the caregiving stress began, about a year after my husband's health deteriorated; before that, I lived a very organized life with checklists and routines. Since then, these difficulties have been pretty much constant, and even when things quiet down slightly, I rarely feel like my old steady self.
Do your concentration and memory problems get noticeably better when the caregiving stress is reduced, or do they stay about the same even during calmer periods?

Since the caregiving responsibilities and stress haven't really stopped, it is hard to say for sure. But even during the brief moments when things quiet down a little, my mind still feels quite jumbled and I struggle to keep things straight.

Do you also notice low mood, anxiety, loss of interest, or feeling emotionally overwhelmed since your husband became ill? Or is the main problem that your memory and thinking have clearly gotten worse compared with before, even without feeling especially depressed or anxious?

The main issue is definitely that my thinking and ability to keep plans straight have gotten much worse, but I don't really feel depressed or down in a typical way. Instead, my mind is constantly racing, and my mood actually shoots way up to where I feel overly cheerful and hyperactive, or suddenly very irritable and snappy if the smallest thing goes wrong.

Have you ever had periods of at least several days when you felt unusually energized or irritable with much less need for sleep, racing thoughts, increased talkativeness, or doing more risky or impulsive things than usual?

Yes, I've had those exact periods on and off for close to ten months now. I feel completely wired and only sleep two or three hours a night without feeling tired, while my mind races and I start scrubbing the bathrooms at three in the morning. I get overly cheerful and full of energy, but then I'll suddenly snap and get incredibly irritable over the smallest things.
During these high-energy periods, have you ever had hallucinations, delusions, or felt like your thoughts were so fast or scattered that other people could not follow you at all?

Yes, during those high-energy times, that man's voice gets much louder and I feel even more convinced that my boss and the hospital are watching and judging me. My mind races so fast with so many thoughts at once that when I try to speak, my words get completely jumbled and I jump from topic to topic, leaving others unable to follow what I'm saying.
During these high-energy periods, do the voices or beliefs about being watched still happen even when your mood is not unusually high or irritable, or only when you are in that elevated state?

Yes, those things still happen even when my mood isn't high or irritable. During quieter weeks when my mood feels flat and I'm not rushing around, I still hear that man's voice telling me they're going to take my husband away, and I stay convinced that my boss and the hospital are secretly watching and judging everything I do.
Have you ever had times when the hearing voices or feeling watched continued for at least 2 weeks while your mood was not unusually high, irritable, or depressed?

Yes, there have definitely been times like that. Even during a couple of quieter weeks when my mood felt flat and I wasn't rushing around, I still heard that man's voice telling me they were going to take my husband away. I also stayed completely convinced during those weeks that my boss and the hospital were secretly watching and judging everything I did.

Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you heard voices or had paranoid beliefs, but you did not have any manic symptoms like decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, or unusually high or irritable mood?

Yes, I have. During a couple of quieter weeks when my mood was flat and I wasn't rushing around or staying up, I still heard that man's voice warning me that people were going to take my husband away. Even then, I remained completely convinced that my boss and the hospital were secretly watching and judging everything I did.
Have you ever had a full manic episode that lasted at least 1 week, with very little sleep, racing thoughts, and unusually high or irritable mood most of the day nearly every day?

Yes, I have been experiencing those intense, wired phases on and off for about ten months now, and they definitely last much longer than just a week. During these times, I only sleep two or three hours a night but feel completely wired, and my mind races so fast with multiple thoughts at once that I can't keep track of them. My mood also swings from feeling overly cheerful and energetic to snapping in anger at the absolute smallest things.
Have you ever had at least 2 weeks of hallucinations or paranoid beliefs when you were not having any manic or depressive symptoms at all?

Yes, I have. Even during a couple of quieter weeks when my mood felt flat and I wasn't rushing around so much, I still heard that man's voice telling me people were going to take my husband away. During those same weeks, I remained completely convinced that the hospital and my boss were secretly watching and judging everything I did.
